transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-01
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Clara Zhou (Redwood CSM); Sarah Lee (Monarch Eng Mgr), Ravi Patel (Monarch SRE), Mina Chen (Monarch Security), Tom Nguyen (Product), Alex Gomez (Data)

Summary:
Quick sync to follow up on last week's reliability incident (spike of 5xx/timeouts during batch run), review recent logs and mitigations, agree on load test and retry/backoff changes, and confirm what Redwood will deliver for diagnostics and compliance.

Topics:
- Incident recap and current status
- Error profiles: 5xx vs timeouts vs rate-limits
- Retry/backoff recommendations and client changes
- KV cache / prefix caching / routing behavior
- Observability: traces, sampling, token-level cost impact
- Next steps and owners

Action items (quick): see metadata list above.

Transcript: (timestamps approximate, auto-generated)
[00:00] Lena: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. um, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes. quick roll call, and then Mateo will walk through what we found in the traces.
[00:10] Sarah: hi, Sarah here. thanks — sorry we had a rough morning with another flaky run, so appreciate the follow up.
[00:15] Ravi: Hey, Ravi — yeah, saw some 502s and a small window of timeouts around 03:12 UTC during yesterday's load.
[00:22] Lena: Got it. Mateo? take it away.
[00:25] Mateo: Yup. so we pulled the request traces from the pilot cluster and matched them to your error logs. what we see in the majority of the failures is a mix: about 60% are 5xx responses from the serving runtime, roughly 25% are client-side timeouts, and the rest are throttle responses from our rate limiter when the burst exceeded the route quota.
[00:45] Mateo: The 5xx pattern is interesting — intermittent OOM-ish stack traces in the runtime, but not a full node crash. likely related to concurrent KV-cache misses + large prefix requests causing memory pressure during peak batching windows.
[01:05] Ravi: Aha, we do have some bigger batched jobs hitting long sequences, that's our nightly enrichment. we thought the rate was lower but the concurrency spiked because of a replay.
[01:18] Tom: just to clarify, the replay was manual? or some automated retry?
[01:22] Alex: it was a backfill we kicked off, parallelism slider was set to 8, maybe should have been 4.
[01:30] Mateo: that helps explain: high concurrency + long sequences = longer KV cache ops and bigger memory working set. on some host kernels that pushes the runtime into higher GC / memory path and yields 5xx. we can tune kernel selection and memory caps on the model variant to reduce the OOM-like behavior.
[01:50] Lena: do you have a quick mitigation we can apply today?
[01:54] Mateo: yes — short term we can do three things: 1) reduce max concurrency per client route (client-side throttle), 2) enable prefix caching for the long-prompt templates so repeats hit the cache, and 3) temporarily bump retry budgets and add exponential backoff on the client side to avoid thundering herd. I'll paste sample curl and client snippets after the call.
[02:15] Ravi: re backoff — we currently do a fixed 1s retry x2 from our worker. is that enough? it wasn't staggered across workers.
[02:25] Mateo: fixed 1s isn't ideal. recommend jittered exponential backoff starting at 250ms, multiplied by 2, with jitter and a max of 5s, and a cap of 3 retries for idempotent enrichment requests. for non-idempotent work we should avoid automatic retries and instead route failures to a dead-letter queue for manual re-run.
[02:45] Sarah: ok that sounds reasonable. how much of this is config on our side vs Redwood changes?
[02:50] Mateo: client retries and concurrency are on your side; we can enable prefix/KV caching and tune the runtime memory caps on our side immediately — those are quick toggles. for longer term we'll propose quantization/model variant changes and kernel selection improvements.
[03:05] Mina: quick security question — enabling prefix cache, what data is stored and for how long? need to confirm it's encrypted at rest and that we can set TTLs per customer.
[03:15] Lena: good call. Mateo, can you cover caching TTL and KMS?
[03:18] Mateo: yeah. prefix cache stores tokenized prefixes (not raw PII strings) in Redis-like in-memory stores. for Private customers we can use customer-managed Redis or our managed cache with encryption at rest; TTLs are configurable per-route, default 24h. keys are anonymized but we can provide an option to opt-out of prefix caching. I'll capture the specifics in the artifact we send.
[03:40] Mina: we'll need the exact encryption-at-rest details and KMS integration notes — also audit log entries for cache access.
[03:47] Lena: noted, Lena will share SOC2 and KMS docs.
[03:50] Clara: i'll add the compliance docs to the case.
[03:53] Ravi: on the rate limiter side, we saw some 429s with a retry-after header missing — is that on Redwood or our proxy?
[04:00] Mateo: the rate limiter should add retry-after in the 429. in this case, the 429s without retry-after were emitted by an upstream component (edge proxy) that returns an immediate 429 when internal quota is hit. we need to correlate timestamps — Mateo to send the filtered traces.
[04:15] Tom: is there a way to prevent the edge from preemptively rejecting? we'd rather have graceful backlog.
[04:20] Mateo: yes — we can adopt a small token-bucket smoothing policy at the edge and set up a short burst window, while the route-level limiter preserves SLOs. that's a config change on the infra stack.
[04:33] Ravi: sounds good. We'll have infra try a token-bucket smoothing tomorrow against a stage cluster.
[04:38] Alex: one other ask — can Redwood provide token-level cost delta for increased retries and caching? Product needs to see ROI vs cost.
[04:45] Lena: yes, Redwood can estimate token-level cost impact; Mateo can run a simulated cost delta after the proposed changes.
[04:50] Mateo: i'll run the sim against your sample traffic and send a spreadsheet. expect approximate % change, and note that prefix caching often reduces token usage significantly for repeated templates.
[05:00] Sarah: on observability, what's best practice for sampling? we lost some traces during the incident.
[05:08] Mateo: increase trace sampling for the route to 100% for the duration of a repro (short window) and then drop to 5% afterwards; also enable request-id propagation and keep the first and last 2k tokens in our logs for a short TTL. we'll redact sensitive fields.
[05:25] Mina: redact how? need to be sure PII is never stored even in short TTL logs.
[05:30] Mateo: our pipeline supports regex-based redaction and PII scrubbers; we'll share the rule set. if you prefer, we can forward traces to your S3 so retention is controlled by you.
[05:42] Ravi: that would be great for forensics.
[05:46] Lena: okay — let's confirm owners. quick recap of technical mitigations:
[05:50] - short term: reduce concurrency on your workers + jittered backoff + enable prefix caching (Mateo to enable and share config)
[05:58] - mid term: increase runtime memory caps or tune kernel selection / model variant (SE + engineering)
[06:04] - infra: token-bucket smoothing at edge to avoid preemptive 429s (Ravi + infra)
[06:10] - observability: raise sampling briefly and share traces to customer's S3 optionally (Mateo + Mina)
[06:16] Lena: And on process next steps: Mateo will send the filtered logs and dev snippets, Lena will share SOC2/KMS docs, Ravi will run load tests, and we'll regroup next week.
[06:26] Tom: one follow up — any immediate config that would block us from continuing the pilot?
[06:30] Mateo: no blockers; the changes are safe to roll in stages. for the most part the client-side concurrency and retries reduce load immediately.
[06:36] Sarah: timeline? can we get the initial artifacts by Wednesday?
[06:40] Lena: yes — we aim to have docs and snippets by 2026-06-03.
[06:45] Mina: please cc my security mailbox (mina@monarchfin.com) when sending compliance docs.
[06:50] Lena: will do.
[06:52] Clara: I'll schedule the next weekly sync for same time next week and add a deep-dive with infra if needed.
[06:58] Ravi: we'll also share the load test results and any infra error logs.
[07:02] Lena: great — anything else?
[07:06] Alex: slight nit — when you send client code make sure language samples include both java and python.
[07:10] Mateo: yes — i'll include python, java, and node.
[07:14] Lena: OK thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
